requirements.title: ACOSPI argument restrictions

pending.acospi-argument-admissible: Future positive controls call ACOSPI with admissible argument types and values from p3. Invalid type or out-of-domain source shapes remain source-control only and carry no local diagnostic expectation because p3 is an unnumbered argument restriction.

requirements.title: ACOSPI mathematical approximation is processor dependent
requirements.source: 16.9.7 p5 approximation clause; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF378.
requirements.definition: The ACOSPI result value is a processor-dependent approximation to the specified inverse cosine function.

pending.acospi-processor-dependent-approximation: No portable oracle may require a particular rounded floating result for the approximation. Future tests may assert only source-fixed bounds or exact characteristics, not exact transcendent values.

requirements.title: ACOSPI result range constraints
requirements.source: 16.9.7 p5 range clause; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF378.
requirements.definition: The ACOSPI result is expressed in half-revolutions and lies in the range 0 <= ACOSPI(X) <= 1.

pending.acospi-result-half-revolutions-range: Future fixture uses admissible real inputs and asserts the result is within [0,1], avoiding exact equality to a processor-dependent approximation except where a later review proves exactness from the source.

review_rationale: Source registration for 16.9 and 16.9.1-16.9.7: ABS, ACHAR, ACOS, ACOSD, ACOSH and ACOSPI (batch179). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. ACHAR's required results for codes 0-127 are split from the processor-dependent cases, and the exact result ranges of the inverse cosine family are split from their processor-dependent approximations; Examples are informative.
